slot_note: Second redraw cell of the round (product-analytics / churn-propensity-uplift-modeling, Forecasting) after architecture v1 (psychology-behavioral-science, a provincial employment service) was spent at Gate F; the seed FC48 world (drop-off recycling bins) died at stage 1 on measurement before any card.
niche: a UK news publisher's forecast of the share of its January at-risk list of monthly digital subscribers that a half-price retention offer keeps through March, carried from last January's half-and-half test after billing moved to the 1st of the month
analyst_test: A strong analyst who joins last January's test arms to the cancellations, reads a subscriber as subscribed on 31 March until the end of the last paid period, fits a two-model or transformed-outcome uplift on the subscriber features and scores this year's list files about 10 per cent, where the share is about 20 per cent.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the retention offer's effect conditional on how many days before a subscriber's next monthly bill it lands, estimated from last January's randomised half-and-half test the way uplift modelling estimates a conditional treatment effect and carried to a list whose bills all fall six days after the send; with patients, reminder letters or tariff notices in place of subscribers the call loses the recurring bill at which a subscriber decides whether to keep paying, the clock the effect runs on, and the two discounted bills it buys.
layer1: the billing platform replaced from the October 2026 bill run: legacy invoices on each subscription's anniversary day in their own layout and identifiers, the new platform's invoices on the 1st with a pro-rated first invoice per migrated subscription, an identifier crosswalk issued
cancellations exported as requests with the end of the paid period, so a subscriber stays live until the last paid day
the email platform's send, open and click log in UTC against the subscription records in UK local time
the offers engine's acceptances keyed by its own customer reference, joined through the crosswalk
partner-paid and staff access set up as ordinary monthly subscriptions, told apart only on the invoices
test accounts and duplicate sends in the campaign tool's exports
plan and price changes over the year, zero-rated VAT on digital news, refunds and credit notes as separate rows
the at-risk lists cut by the retention model on their own dates, with its score and band
stakeholder_role: head of subscriber retention in the audience revenue team

spine.entity: one line of a legacy invoice raised on a subscription's billing day (the plan's charge, a discount or a credit), for the subscriptions on either retention list and their add-ons
spine.grain: invoice line (subscription x bill date x line type)
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a legacy subscription billing system's invoice line export)

driver: An intervention moves a unit mainly when it lands in the days before the unit's own recurring decision, so the effect a randomised test measured while those decisions fell at every point of the units' cycles is an average over the cycle, and it does not carry to a delivery that now lands a few days before every unit's decision; only the effect the test read on its units whose decision fell as close to their delivery does.
driver_concrete: A half-price retention offer keeps a subscriber mainly when it lands in the fortnight before their next monthly bill, so last January's half-and-half test, sent while bills fell on every day of the month, kept about 9 in 100 across the cycle, while this January's list, every bill on 1 February six days after the send since billing moved to the 1st, is kept at the rate the test measured on subscribers billed within two weeks of it, about 20 in 100.
stump: An uplift model on last January's half-and-half test (two-model or transformed outcome on the subscriber features) scored on this year's list files about 10 per cent; the test's subscribers whose next bill fell within two weeks of the send were kept at about twice the overall rate and almost none of the rest, and every bill on this year's list falls six days after the send, so the share is about 20 per cent.

differentiation.task167: task167 infers which of two unnamed drawdown schedules each unit follows from its own first-year draws; here no per-unit schedule is inferred: a randomised offer's effect is read by how many days before each subscriber's next bill it landed and carried to a list the billing calendar has put six days before every bill.
differentiation.task31: task31 splits a lag absolutely on a prior approval with the same counterparty, a standing property recovered through a multi-file join; here the split is the days between the offer's delivery and each subscriber's own next bill, which no record of the subscriber holds and which the move to billing on the 1st set for the whole target at once.
differentiation.task44: task44 decomposes a pilot's pooled gain over a behavioural moderator, a trait of each unit measured over a prior window; here the moderator is not a trait at all but where the unit's own recurring bill falls relative to the delivery, so one subscriber is persuadable one fortnight and not the next, and the target's position comes from the billing calendar.
differentiation.task56: task56 restores a population billed on a different basis that is known only by its absence from the event streams; here nobody is missing or restored: every list member is present, and the effect each is credited with turns on the days from the send to their next bill.
differentiation.task57: task57 v19 separates candidate measures that reproduce their own year by identity, on a held-out year; here no measure is chosen by a back-test: a randomised effect is conditioned on where the delivery fell in each subscriber's billing cycle.
differentiation.task76: task76 cuts a forward count by a class with zero observed conversion rebuilt from a log of failed contacts; here no class has zero conversion: the offer converts well when it lands within two weeks of the bill and hardly at all before that, and the forecast list sits wholly in the first band.
differentiation.task124: task124 prices newcomers from analogs whose measured value the organisation's own dispatch held down; here no evidence is suppressed by an intervention: the evidence is a randomised test whose effect varies with the delivery's place in each subscriber's billing cycle.

lineage.niche: a provincial employment service's forecast of the share of jobseekers' own contacts its upgraded digital assistant takes in the eight weeks after an assistant-first period, from each claimant's contact-by-contact channel choices and the outcomes they met
lineage.driver: Experiences a unit did not choose move its later choices far less than experiences it chose, so a period that sends every unit to one option converts few of them; the record holds those imposed experiences only as scattered single episodes, so a learner fitted to the whole record with one rate over-predicts the conversion, and only a separate rate for the imposed experiences, read from those episodes, carries to the period.
lineage.driver_concrete: Jobseekers sent to the digital assistant when the phone queue overflows learn about a fifth as much from it as those who open it themselves, so the eight assistant-first weeks, which send every call to the assistant, lift claimants' own use of it in March and April far less than a reinforcement-learning model with one learning rate predicts.
lineage.stump: One learning rate fitted to every contact and simulated through the assistant-first weeks files about 40 per cent of claimants' own contacts in the assistant for March and April; the overflow-redirected contacts in the record teach about a fifth as much as chosen ones, so the share is about 26 per cent.
lineage.answer: 25 per cent (to the nearest 5 per cent; 25.21 unrounded)
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 Gate F on target.zip 3be16ba3 (2026-10-21): the re-judge was DETERMINISTIC and APPROVE, but scored reader I landed the 25 bin with a fitted outcome-weighted habit model (decay 0.63 per contact, weights by the previous contact outcome) that never separated the imposed contacts; whole per cent had failed determinism and nearest 5 admitted the neighbour, so the lever was no wider than the golden family spread
